title: The Network Takes a Cut
audience: Short-video audience, phones first; a 30-second paper-cut explainer of how Uber earns money
tone: plain, quick, a little wry — a business explainer that never sounds like an advert
logline: Uber does not own the ride; it owns the match, and takes a cut of every match it makes.

spine.want: to understand how a company with almost no cars makes money
spine.obstacle: the obvious answer — it owns the cars — is wrong
spine.turn: the fare is only one of the things the network sells
spine.button: the network gets stronger as both sides grow, which is why it is hard to leave

narration.text: Uber does not own the cars, kitchens, or the freight it moves; it owns the network that connects them.
Riders open the app, drivers use their own cars, and every completed trip is matched by the platform.
Uber takes a service fee from every fare; the driver keeps the rest, and the platform keeps the match.
The app sells delivery, freight, advertising and memberships, so one network earns in more than one way.
More riders make each car busier, more drivers shorten the wait, and the network gets harder to leave.
